description: Chat with any machine over SSH: prompts run as commands on the remote host, with multiplexed sessions, a working directory that survives between turns, and pinned host-key verification.

A configured connection grants shell access to the host it names. BrainBoost Ltd. is not responsible for any damages, losses, or issues resulting from its use.

sections.title: SSH
sections.text: Turn a chat into a shell on any reachable machine, using the OpenSSH client already installed on the host.
list: Config fields: host, port, username, authentication (agent, key path, pasted key, or password), key passphrase, known hosts, pinned host key fingerprint, working directory, shell, session persistence, and timeouts
Output: Response text, stdout, stderr, exit code, working directory, session ID, host, and status.

sections.title: Typical workflow
sections.intro: Configure the host and credentials, then run commands on it as part of a BrainBoost pipeline.

cards.title: Connect
cards.text: Name the host, port and remote account. Reuse the running ssh-agent by default, or supply a key or password. Pin the host key fingerprint to refuse any other key.

cards.title: Fetch
cards.text: Send a command as a chat message. The first turn opens a multiplexed connection; later turns reuse it, and cd carries forward between them.

cards.title: Consume
cards.text: Consume stdout, stderr, exit code and working directory from the chat UI or downstream automation.

items.q: What do I need to configure?
items.a: A reachable host, a remote username, and a way to authenticate. With the default agent method, no secret is stored in Subjective at all. OpenSSH 8.4 or newer must be installed on the machine running the datasource.
A password or key passphrase is written to a private file read by a generated askpass helper and removed when the turn ends. Secrets never appear in command lines, logs, transcripts, or results.
Returns response text, stdout, stderr, exit code, the resulting working directory, the session ID, and a status such as completed, command_failed, authentication_required, or host_key_mismatch.
Outputs are emitted to downstream subscribers in the BrainBoost pipeline. Some datasources also write artifacts (context files, catalogs, or exports) locally based on your configuration.

sections.text: Add it to your BrainBoost pipeline and start ingesting.
sections.subtext: Run this datasource locally with your own credentials and storage.
